title: Neo4j
summary: A property graph database option with Cypher queries.

sections.label: Documented role
sections.text: Neo4j describes a property graph model and its Cypher query language.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: Selecting Neo4j records the technology and version. Atlas currently adds generic component questions. The RDF and SPARQL profile is not applied merely because this is a graph database.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm the actual version, supported interface, permissions, data model and expected query results. Compare alternatives using your constraints.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Architecture and impact, Development, Tests and review. Use for an affected Neo4j property-graph interface when choosing the model, implementing the query boundary and checking actual results. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Record actual Neo4j and driver versions, graph model, approved interface and caller scope.
Check output to obtain: Compare expected nodes and relationships with observed Cypher results for bounded normal, empty and denied cases.
Check output to obtain: Record unresolved compatibility explicitly. Do not substitute RDF or SPARQL expectations for the actual property-graph contract.

confidence: Documented facts have scoped sources. Suitability for a particular project remains unverified.

catalog.applicability: Use this technology example when your data is a property graph queried with Cypher. Atlas records the technology and version and adds generic component questions, the RDF and SPARQL profile is not applied just because Neo4j is a graph database.
